newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen slowing ahead of support.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen slowing ahead of support.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower turnover after a one-session growth and analysts saw them at least slowing falls in the next two sessions with 16,000 points providing strong support.
The main market's WIG index fell 1.1 percent, to 16,244.2, and turnover fell 13.5 percent to 152.6 million zlotys ($50.3 million) on all three markets as 62 issues fell, 22 rose and 14 were flat.
"The market should slow in the next two days as we are approaching 16,000 points, where demand should appear," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.

Analysts said in the longer-term the bourse was likely to continue its eight-week sideways drift as some investors were scaling-down buying ahead of September elections but Poland's strong macroeconomic outlook was limiting the downside.

Mass privatisation NFI units jumped 5.9 percent in heavy trade after finance minister said he might drop plans to levy tax on profits made through sales of firms by NFIs and after the NFIs showed profits in the first quarter of 1997.
Some analysts said, amid the expected horizontal trend falls were more likely as large attractive offers on the primary market were seen drawing capital from the bourse.
Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy offer is due late May with its retail tranche estimated at about 500 million zlotys ($161 million), while copper giant KGHM sale is seen in June.

Analysts said banks, which fell significantly in the last three months were looking attractive at current prices, which might spur some bargain-hunting, but expected a strong rebound only if their earnings improved, which they saw in 1998.
Two largest listed banks Bank Slaski and Band Przemyslowo-Handlowy both fell about 30 percent from 52-week highs in early February. REUTERS
